title: Kernel of a monoid-algebra quotient induced by a congruence
statement: Let $M$ be a commutative monoid, written additively, and let $c$ be a monoid congruence on $M$, meaning an equivalence relation on $M$ such that $c(u,v)$ implies $c(u+w,v+w)$ for all $w\in M$. Write $c.\operatorname{Quotient}$ for the commutative monoid of $c$-equivalence classes and $q:M\to c.\operatorname{Quotient}$ for the quotient homomorphism. Let $A$ be a commutative ring. For a commutative monoid $N$ write $A[N]$ for its monoid algebra: the free $A$-module with basis symbols $[n]$, $n\in N$, with the $A$-bilinear multiplication determined by $[n][n']=[n+n']$ and unit $[0]$. The homomorphism $q$ induces the $A$-algebra homomorphism $A[M]\to A[c.\operatorname{Quotient}]$, $[m]\mapsto[q(m)]$. Its kernel is the ideal generated by all differences $[u]-[v]$ with $c(u,v)$. If $c$ is the smallest congruence containing a set $S\subseteq M\times M$ (the intersection of all congruences containing $S$), this kernel is already generated by the differences $[u]-[v]$ for $(u,v)\in S$.

source.place: Supporting quotient facts only: Con.mk'_ker (line 154, the kernel of the quotient homomorphism is c) and Con.lift / Con.lift_mk' (lines 195--213); the monoid-algebra kernel formula itself is not stated there and remains to be proved when this node is split.

proof.text: Write $B=A[M]$, $Q=c.\operatorname{Quotient}$ and $\phi:B\to A[Q]$ for the given map. Let $I$ be the ideal generated by $[u]-[v]$ for $c(u,v)$. Since $q(u)=q(v)$ for such a pair, $\phi([u]-[v])=[q(u)]-[q(v)]=0$. Every element of $I$ is a finite sum $\sum_i h_i([u_i]-[v_i])$ with $h_i\in B$ and $c(u_i,v_i)$. Applying $\phi$ gives $\sum_i\phi(h_i)0=0$, so $I\subseteq\ker\phi$.

source.place: Definition of the ideal generated by a set and the quotient equivalence relation; direct calculation.

proof.text: Take $f\in\ker\phi$ and write its finite basis expansion $f=\sum_{m\in T}a_m[m]$, where $T\subset M$ is finite. Put $C=q(T)$ and $T_z=\{m\in T:q(m)=z\}$ for $z\in C$. These finite subsets partition $T$: each $m\in T$ lies in the unique subset indexed by $z=q(m)$. Thus $\phi(f)=\sum_{z\in C}b_z[z]$, where $b_z=\sum_{m\in T_z}a_m$. This equality is obtained by assigning each summand $a_m[q(m)]$ to its unique index $q(m)$. The coefficient of $[z]$ in the zero element $\phi(f)$ is zero, so $b_z=0$ for every $z\in C$.

source.place: Free-module coefficients and finite partition of the support; compare Finsupp.mapDomain_apply_eq_sum, Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Basic.lean:1432-1434.

proof.text: For each $z\in C$ choose $r_z\in T_z$, possible because $z\in q(T)$. For $m\in T_z$ one has $q(m)=q(r_z)$ and hence $c(m,r_z)$ by the definition of quotient classes. Distributivity gives the explicit identity $\sum_{m\in T_z}a_m[m]=\sum_{m\in T_z}a_m([m]-[r_z])+\bigl(\sum_{m\in T_z}a_m\bigr)[r_z]$. Indeed, expanding the right-hand side cancels the two sums of terms $a_m[r_z]$. The last term is $b_z[r_z]=0$ by step 2.

source.place: Quotient equivalence classes (compare AddCon.mk'_ker, Mathlib/GroupTheory/Congruence/Hom.lean:154); finite distributivity and cancellation.

proof.text: Each $[m]-[r_z]$ in step 3 is a generator of $I$. Multiplication by $a_m[0]\in B$ gives $a_m([m]-[r_z])\in I$, since $[0]$ is the multiplicative unit. Adding these terms over $m\in T_z$ and then over $z\in C$ expresses $f$ as an element of $I$. If $T$ is empty, $f=0\in I$ and neither a representative nor a nonempty class is needed. We have proved $\ker\phi\subseteq I$, and together with step 1 this proves the first kernel formula.

source.place: Finite-sum identity of step 3 and the defining closure properties of an ideal.

proof.text: Now suppose $c$ is the smallest congruence containing $S$. Let $J$ be the ideal generated by $[u]-[v]$ with $(u,v)\in S$. Because $S\subseteq c$, its generators belong to $I$, and every finite $B$-linear combination of them belongs to $I$; hence $J\subseteq I$. Define a relation $d$ on $M$ by $d(u,v)\iff [u]-[v]\in J$. It is reflexive because $[u]-[u]=0\in J$, symmetric because $[v]-[u]=-([u]-[v])$, and transitive because $[u]-[w]=([u]-[v])+([v]-[w])$ and an ideal is closed under addition.

source.place: Definitions of generated ideal, smallest congruence, and equivalence relation; displayed ring identities.

proof.text: The relation $d$ is preserved by addition: if $[u]-[v]\in J$ and $w\in M$, then $[u+w]-[v+w]=[w]([u]-[v])\in J$ by the monoid-algebra multiplication rule and the ideal property. Thus $d$ is a monoid congruence. Every $(u,v)\in S$ satisfies $d(u,v)$ because its difference generates $J$. By the defining minimality of $c$ among congruences containing $S$, it follows that $c\subseteq d$.

source.place: The definition of monoid congruence and the explicit translation identity; no cancellation in M is used.

proof.text: Consequently every generator $[u]-[v]$ of $I$, with $c(u,v)$, lies in $J$. Every element of $I$ is a finite sum of multiples of such generators, so closure of $J$ under multiplication and addition gives $I\subseteq J$. Combining this with step 5 yields $I=J$. Substituting into the kernel equality of steps 1-4 gives $\ker\phi=J$, exactly the assertion for a generating set $S$.

source.place: Definitions of generated ideal and d; conclusion from steps 4-6.

proof_origin.place: Con.mk'_ker / AddCon.mk'_ker, quotient equivalence relation only. The finite-support kernel proof and generated-congruence argument are written by Q44; this file is not claimed to contain the monoid-algebra theorem.

lean.statement: theorem congruence_polynomial_kernel {M : Type u} {A : Type v} [AddCommMonoid M] [CommRing A] (c : AddCon M) : RingHom.ker (AddMonoidAlgebra.mapDomainRingHom A c.mk') = Ideal.span {x : AddMonoidAlgebra A M | ∃ u w : M, c u w ∧ x = AddMonoidAlgebra.of' A M u - AddMonoidAlgebra.of' A M w} ∧ ∀ S : Set (M × M), c = addConGen (fun u w => (u, w) ∈ S) → RingHom.ker (AddMonoidAlgebra.mapDomainRingHom A c.mk') = Ideal.span {x : AddMonoidAlgebra A M | ∃ p : M × M, p ∈ S ∧ x = AddMonoidAlgebra.of' A M p.1 - AddMonoidAlgebra.of' A M p.2}
